guidance: Plough the field to a depth of 20-25 cm using a tractor or power tiller. Break clods and level the field uniformly. Apply farmyard manure at 12.5 tonnes per hectare and incorporate into the soil before puddling.
government_recommendation: Use certified paddy varieties recommended by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) such as ADT 43 or CO 51.

guidance: Level the field using a laser leveller or traditional float board to ensure uniform water distribution. Strengthen bunds to a height of 20-25 cm to prevent water loss. Check for mole rat burrows and seal immediately.
government_recommendation: Strengthen field bunds before transplanting to retain irrigation water as per TNAU guidelines.

guidance: Select certified seeds of high-yielding varieties such as ADT 43, CO 51, or IR 64. Treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens at 10 g per kg seed. Perform salt water test: discard seeds that float; use only seeds that sink.
government_recommendation: Use seeds certified by Tamil Nadu Seed Certification Authority to ensure purity and germination above 85%.

guidance: Prepare raised nursery beds of 1 metre width and 10 metres length. Apply 5 kg of well-decomposed compost per bed. Sow pre-germinated seeds at 100 g per square metre. Cover with paddy straw to retain moisture and protect from birds.
government_recommendation: Apply Trichoderma viride at 5 g per kg seed before sowing as per Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department advisory.

guidance: Maintain thin water film in nursery. Irrigate twice daily using watering can in early stage. Remove weeds manually at 10th day after sowing. Apply DAP solution at 1% as foliar spray on 12th day to boost seedling vigour.
government_recommendation: Ensure nursery beds are free from shade and receive minimum 6 hours of direct sunlight daily.

guidance: Transplant 21-25 day old seedlings with 2-3 seedlings per hill. Maintain spacing of 20 cm x 15 cm. Transplant at a shallow depth of 2-3 cm. Avoid deep planting as it delays tillering. Complete transplanting within 3-4 days.
government_recommendation: Follow recommended spacing of 20x15 cm for medium duration varieties and 20x20 cm for long duration varieties as per TNAU norms.

guidance: Maintain 2-5 cm standing water from transplanting to tillering stage. Apply first dose of nitrogen at 50 kg urea per hectare at 10-12 days after transplanting. Apply potassium chloride at 50 kg per hectare to promote tillering.
government_recommendation: Apply nitrogen fertilizer in split doses: 50% basal
column18: 25% at panicle initiation to avoid lodging.

guidance: Apply pre-emergence herbicide Butachlor at 1.5 kg active ingredient per hectare within 3-5 days of transplanting. Maintain standing water for 3 days after herbicide application. Do manual weeding at 25 and 45 days after transplanting.
government_recommendation: Use integrated weed management combining pre-emergence herbicide and one hand weeding for effective control.

guidance: Maintain standing water at 5 cm depth during vegetative phase. Drain field intermittently every 10 days for 2-3 days to improve soil aeration and root development. Avoid water stress especially during tillering and panicle initiation.
government_recommendation: Follow Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD) technique recommended by TNAU to save water up to 30% without yield loss.

guidance: Apply second dose of nitrogen at 50 kg urea per hectare at active tillering stage (30-35 days after transplanting). Foliar spray zinc sulphate at 0.5% if zinc deficiency symptoms appear. Top dress with potash at 30 kg per hectare.
government_recommendation: Conduct soil test before crop season and adjust fertilizer doses based on soil nutrient status as per TNAU soil health card.

activity: Stem Borer and Leaf Folder Monitoring
guidance: Inspect paddy fields every 5-7 days for stem borer infestation. Count dead hearts in vegetative stage and white ears in reproductive stage. Install pheromone traps at 5 per acre. If dead heart incidence exceeds 5%, apply Chlorpyrifos 2.5% dust at 25 kg per hectare.
government_recommendation: Use Integrated Pest Management (IPM) approach. Release Trichogramma japonicum at 5 lakh per hectare at weekly intervals from 30 days after transplanting.

guidance: Scout for paddy blast symptoms on leaves: diamond-shaped grey lesions with brown border. For sheath blight: oval/irregular lesions on lower sheaths. If blast incidence is observed, spray Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g per litre. For sheath blight spray Validamycin at 2 ml per litre.
government_recommendation: Avoid excess nitrogen application as it increases blast susceptibility. Grow blast-resistant varieties like ADT 45 and CO 51.

guidance: At panicle initiation (45-50 days after transplanting), apply third nitrogen dose at 25 kg urea per hectare. Maintain 5 cm water level during booting and heading stage. Avoid any nitrogen application after panicle initiation as it causes lodging.
government_recommendation: Apply micronutrient mixture foliar spray at booting stage to improve grain filling and reduce unfilled grains.

guidance: Monitor flowering (anthesis) during early morning hours (8-10 AM). Ensure no water stress during pollination. If dry spells occur, immediately irrigate the field. Observe panicle emergence and note any sterility. Scout for brown plant hopper during this stage.
government_recommendation: Release egg parasitoid Trichogramma chilonis to manage lepidopteran pests during flowering stage.

guidance: Drain the paddy field completely at 15-20 days before harvest to allow field to dry and facilitate combine harvester movement. Observe grain colour change from green to golden yellow as maturity indicator. Ensure 80% of grains are golden yellow before harvest.
government_recommendation: Drain field 2 weeks before harvest to harden soil and reduce post-harvest moisture content in grains.

guidance: Harvest paddy when 80-85% of grains turn golden yellow. Use combine harvester or sickle for harvesting. Harvest during morning hours to reduce shattering loss. Maintain moisture content between 20-22% at harvest for safe storage after drying.
government_recommendation: Avail custom hiring of combine harvester from TNAU Farm Machinery Training Centre or cooperative societies to reduce harvest loss below 3%.

guidance: Thresh harvested paddy within 24 hours to prevent grain deterioration. Dry grains on clean cemented floor or tarpaulin to reduce moisture content to 14% for safe storage. Avoid drying on bare ground to prevent contamination and aflatoxin development.
government_recommendation: Use mechanical dryer or solar dryer available through Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department subsidy scheme for efficient grain drying.

guidance: Plough the field to a depth of 25-30 cm to break compacted subsoil layers. This allows peg penetration and pod development. Apply gypsum at 400 kg per hectare as basal to prevent calcium deficiency in pods. Level and prepare fine tilth.
government_recommendation: Apply gypsum mandatorily at pegging stage in Erode and Coimbatore districts where calcium-deficient red soils are common.

guidance: Select bold-seeded varieties such as TMV 2, VRI 2, or GPBD 4 for rainfed areas. Shell the pods just before sowing to maintain seed viability. Treat seeds with Thiram at 3 g per kg seed. Inoculate with Rhizobium culture at 25 g per kg seed.
government_recommendation: Use Rhizobium inoculation mandatorily for groundnut to enhance biological nitrogen fixation and reduce fertilizer cost.

guidance: Sow groundnut seeds at a spacing of 30 cm between rows and 10 cm between plants for bunch types. Sowing depth should be 5 cm. Sow at onset of monsoon or after soil moisture is adequate. Avoid sowing in waterlogged conditions.
government_recommendation: Sow groundnut at recommended seed rate of 100 kg per hectare for bunch varieties and 80 kg per hectare for spreading types.

guidance: Apply first dose of fertilizer at sowing: 25 kg nitrogen, 50 kg phosphorus, and 75 kg potassium per hectare. Carry out first weeding at 15-20 days after sowing using hand hoe. Maintain plant population by gap filling within 10 days of emergence.
government_recommendation: Apply phosphorus as single superphosphate to meet both phosphorus and sulphur requirement of groundnut crop.

guidance: Apply irrigation at critical stages: germination, flowering, pegging, and pod development. Maintain 60-65% field capacity. Avoid waterlogging. In Salem district red loamy soils, irrigate at 5-7 day intervals. Total water requirement is 400-550 mm per season.
government_recommendation: Use drip irrigation with 60% water saving. Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department provides 50% subsidy on drip irrigation systems.

guidance: Apply gypsum at 400 kg per hectare as band placement near plant rows at pegging stage (30-35 days after sowing). This provides calcium and sulphur directly to developing pods and prevents empty pod syndrome common in Erode district soils.
expected_outcome: Reduced Empty Pods; Better Kernel Quality
government_recommendation: Mandatory gypsum application at pegging stage in calcium-deficient soils of Erode and Coimbatore districts as per TNAU recommendation.

guidance: Monitor flower initiation at 25-30 days after sowing. Apply foliar spray of boron at 0.1% during flowering to improve pod set. Scout for thrips and leaf miner during this stage. Maintain optimum soil moisture for peg penetration.
government_recommendation: Spray boron 0.1% solution during early flowering stage to prevent flower drop and improve pod set.

guidance: Inspect leaves weekly for leaf miner damage (wavy transparent mines on upper leaf surface). Yellow sticky traps at 10 per acre for thrips monitoring. If leaf miner incidence exceeds 5 mines per leaf, spray Spinosad 45 SC at 0.3 ml per litre water.
government_recommendation: Release Chrysoperla carnea at 50000 eggs per hectare as biological control agent for groundnut leaf miner.

activity: Early and Late Leaf Spot Monitoring
guidance: Scout for circular brown spots (early leaf spot) on upper leaf surface from 30th day. For late leaf spot: dark brown spots on lower surface. If 30% leaf area is affected spray Mancozeb 75 WP at 2 g per litre. Repeat at 10-day intervals.
risk_factor: Early Leaf Spot; Late Leaf Spot
government_recommendation: Apply protective fungicide spray schedule starting from 30 days after sowing for leaf spot management in Erode and Salem districts.

guidance: Check pod maturity by observing brown discolouration of inner pod wall. Pull out 5-10 plants and check pod development. 75-80% pods should be mature (inner wall dark brown). Stop irrigation 7-10 days before harvest to facilitate easy harvesting.
government_recommendation: Harvest groundnut at correct maturity to prevent aflatoxin contamination which is a major quality concern in Tamil Nadu export groundnut.

guidance: Harvest when 75-80% pods are mature. Use hand hoe or groundnut digger to uproot plants. In mechanized harvesting, use tractor-mounted digger. Dry the plants in windrows for 2-3 days before stripping pods. Avoid prolonged field drying to prevent aflatoxin.
government_recommendation: Use TNAU-designed groundnut harvesting implements available at TNAU farm machinery outlets to reduce harvest losses below 5%.

guidance: Dry groundnut pods to safe moisture content of 8-9% for storage. Store in gunny bags on raised platforms in well-ventilated godowns. Treat stored pods with Aluminum phosphide at 3 tablets per tonne to prevent storage pests. Avoid mixing with old stock.
government_recommendation: Use Tamil Nadu State Warehousing Corporation facilities for bulk storage to maintain quality and access government procurement schemes.

guidance: Plough the field to a depth of 30-35 cm using disc plough. Subsoil ploughing at 45-60 cm every 3 years improves drainage. Apply FYM at 50 tonnes per hectare and incorporate well into soil. Prepare flat beds or furrows 90 cm apart for planting.
government_recommendation: In Erode and Coimbatore districts use deep ploughing followed by subsoil ploughing as per Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department recommendation for higher ratoon yields.

guidance: Select disease-free two-budded setts from 8-10 month old healthy crop. Treat setts with Aresin (Monolinuron) at 0.1% solution for 15 minutes or with hot water treatment at 52°C for 30 minutes. Use varieties CO 86032 or CO 0212 for high sucrose content.
government_recommendation: Use heat-treated setts to eliminate ratoon stunting disease which causes significant yield loss in Tamil Nadu sugarcane belt.

guidance: Plant setts end to end in furrows at a depth of 8-10 cm. Maintain row spacing of 90 cm for plant crop and 75 cm for ratoon. Apply 25 kg nitrogen, 62.5 kg phosphorus, and 62.5 kg potassium per hectare as basal. Cover setts with 5 cm soil and irrigate immediately.
government_recommendation: Apply basal dose of fertilizer in the furrow before placing setts. Plant crop in January-February for highest yield potential in Erode district.

guidance: From 60-120 days, sugarcane enters rapid growth phase. Apply 100 kg nitrogen per hectare at 60 days and 100 kg at 90 days. Earth up rows at 60 days to support stalk. Irrigation at 7-10 day intervals. Apply Sett Germination Promoter for poor germination areas.
government_recommendation: Apply nitrogen in three equal splits: at planting
column18: and at 90 days to ensure steady nutrient supply during vegetative growth.

guidance: Irrigate sugarcane at 7-day intervals in summer and 10-14 day intervals in winter. Critical periods: germination, tillering, grand growth, and maturity. Avoid waterlogging as it causes root rot. Drip irrigation saves 40% water and improves yield by 20-25% in Erode red soil areas.
government_recommendation: Adopt drip irrigation with 50% subsidy available under Tamil Nadu Micro Irrigation Scheme. Drip-fertigation increases sucrose percentage significantly.

guidance: Apply potassium chloride at 62.5 kg per hectare at 60 days. In Coimbatore soils apply sulphur at 25 kg per hectare. Spray liquid urea at 2% solution at 60 and 90 days for quick nitrogen supply during grand growth. Monitor for iron and manganese deficiency in alkaline soils.
government_recommendation: Adopt fertigation through drip system to supply nutrients precisely during critical growth stages for maximum yield potential.

activity: Early Shoot Borer and Internode Borer Monitoring
guidance: Inspect sugarcane weekly for dead heart caused by early shoot borer. Count attacked shoots per plot. If incidence exceeds 5%, apply Chlorpyrifos granules at 10 kg per hectare in soil. For internode borer release Cotesia flavipes parasitoid at 5000 per hectare.
government_recommendation: Adopt biological control using Trichogramma chilonis egg cards at 5 cards per hectare per week from 60 days after planting.

activity: Red Rot and Smut Disease Monitoring
guidance: Scout for red rot (internal reddening of stalks with fermented smell) and smut whips (black soot-like spores at growing point). Rogue out affected plants immediately. Maintain field sanitation. Treat setts with Carbendazim 0.05% for red rot prevention.
government_recommendation: Use resistant varieties such as CO 7201 and Co 86032 in disease-endemic areas of Erode and Salem districts.

guidance: Stop irrigation 30-45 days before harvest to improve sucrose percentage. Apply Ethephon (2-CEPA) at 50 ppm as chemical ripener 45 days before harvest to increase sugar recovery. Survey cane for mill supply and arrange for timely transport.
government_recommendation: Apply chemical ripener as per Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department advisory to improve Commercial Cane Sugar (CCS) percentage above 10.

guidance: Harvest cane at optimum maturity. Use manual cutting at ground level to leave healthy stubble for ratoon. Remove dried leaves (trash) without burning. Bundle cane and transport to factory within 24 hours to prevent sucrose deterioration. Avoid harvesting wet cane.
government_recommendation: Submit cane to nearest cooperative sugar factory within the harvest schedule allotted by Tamil Nadu Sugar Corporation to ensure fair price and timely payment.

guidance: Dig pits of 60 cm x 60 cm x 60 cm at spacing of 1.8 m x 1.8 m for Grand Naine variety. In Erode district, 3 m x 3 m spacing for robust growth. Fill pits with topsoil mixed with FYM at 10 kg per pit and Neem cake at 200 g per pit. Apply Biofertilizers.
expected_outcome: Good Soil Base for Root Development
government_recommendation: Follow TNAU recommendation of 1.5 m x 1.5 m spacing for Robusta and 1.8 m x 1.8 m for Grand Naine under tissue culture planting.

activity: Suckers or Tissue Culture Plant Selection
guidance: Select sword suckers of 1.5-2 kg weight from disease-free mother plants for conventional planting. For tissue culture banana, procure certified plants from government-approved laboratories. Preferred varieties: Grand Naine for export, Robusta for local market, Poovan for Tamil Nadu market.
government_recommendation: Use tissue culture banana plants certified by Department of Horticulture to ensure disease-free planting material and uniform growth.

guidance: Trim the roots of suckers and remove dry leaves. Plant at the centre of the pit. Cover with soil up to the collar region. Do not plant deep. Irrigate immediately after planting. In Coimbatore district, apply cow dung slurry around base to promote root growth.
government_recommendation: Treat sucker base with Carbendazim 0.1% solution before planting to prevent early fungal infection at planting hole.

guidance: Apply first dose of fertilizer at 30 days: 100 g urea, 100 g superphosphate, and 200 g muriate of potash per plant. Mulch the basin with paddy straw or dry leaves to conserve moisture. Remove pest-damaged leaves immediately. Stake young plants if needed.
government_recommendation: Apply split doses of fertilizers at monthly intervals. Total fertilizer requirement: 200 g N
column18: and 300 g K per plant per crop cycle.

guidance: Banana requires 1200-1500 mm water per crop. Apply water through drip at 12-15 litre per plant per day during summer. Reduce to 8-10 litre during monsoon. Critical stages: shoot establishment, shooting, and bunch filling. Avoid standing water as it causes Fusarium wilt.
expected_outcome: Healthy Root System; Improved Bunch Weight
government_recommendation: Install drip irrigation with fertigation system. Government of Tamil Nadu provides 90% subsidy for drip irrigation in horticulture crops.

guidance: Inspect banana plants for weevil attack: oozing of dark fluid from pseudo stem base. Insert fresh cross-cut sucker pieces as trap and collect weevils. For nematode management, apply Carbofuran granules at 25 g per plant at planting and at 4 months.
government_recommendation: Apply TNAU-recommended biocontrol agent Beauveria bassiana at 5 g per plant for banana weevil management in Erode banana belt.

guidance: Scout for Panama wilt: yellowing and wilting of older leaves progressing inwards. Rogue out affected plants. Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens at 20 g per plant as soil drench. For Sigatoka leaf spot (yellow streaks on leaves) spray Propiconazole 0.1% at 30-day intervals.
government_recommendation: Avoid replanting banana in Panama wilt-affected fields for at least 3 years. Grow resistant variety Nendran in affected areas.

guidance: After shooting, remove the male bud (bell) 15 cm below the last bunch hand. Cover the bunch with blue perforated polythene sleeve to protect from thrips and improve finger development. Remove dried leaves (dedica) around bunch. Apply potash at 100 g per plant after shooting.
expected_outcome: Improved Bunch Size and Fruit Quality
government_recommendation: Bundle bunches with polythene sleeve immediately after emergence to protect from pests and improve size and colour as per export quality standards.

guidance: Check banana maturity by finger angularity. Harvest when fingers change from angular to round shape. Cut one finger from last hand and check for creamy white colour inside. Days to harvest from shooting: Grand Naine 90-100 days, Robusta 100-110 days, Poovan 120-135 days.
government_recommendation: Grade bunches as A
column18: C class before selling. Avoid harvesting immature bunches as they affect market reputation and price.

guidance: Cut bunch with sharp curved knife leaving 30 cm of stalk. Handle with care to avoid bruising. Wash with clean water to remove latex. Grade by weight: Grade A above 18 kg, Grade B 12-18 kg, Grade C below 12 kg. Pack in ventilated crates for transport.
government_recommendation: Contact nearby banana marketing cooperative or HOPCOMS for better price. Government cold storage facilities available in Erode district for value addition.

guidance: After main crop harvest, select one healthy sword sucker for ratoon crop. Remove all other suckers. Apply FYM at 10 kg and neem cake at 200 g to the pit. Ratoon crop requires 70-80% of main crop inputs and gives harvest in 9-10 months.
government_recommendation: Maintain maximum 2 ratoon crops to avoid disease buildup. Replant with fresh tissue culture plants after 2 ratoons.

guidance: Deep summer ploughing to 30-35 cm to expose soil-borne pupae and insects to sunlight. Apply FYM at 12.5 tonnes per hectare. Level the field and form ridges at 60 cm spacing. In Coimbatore black cotton soil areas, avoid deep ploughing when soil is wet.
government_recommendation: Conduct summer deep ploughing at least 4-6 weeks before sowing to disrupt soil-borne pest life cycles and improve aeration.

guidance: Select recommended Bt hybrid cotton varieties: MRC 7377, RCH 2 BG II, or NCS 855 for Tamil Nadu conditions. Treat seeds with Imidacloprid 70 WS at 7 g per kg seed for sucking pest protection. Inoculate with Azospirillum at 25 g per kg seed.
risk_factor: Thrips; Aphid Attack at Seedling Stage
government_recommendation: Use only approved Bt cotton hybrids listed by Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department. Avoid unapproved hybrids that may not be suitable for Tamil Nadu climate.

guidance: Sow cotton seeds at 2-3 seeds per hill at a depth of 3-4 cm. Maintain spacing of 90 cm x 60 cm for hybrid cotton. Apply basal dose of 25 kg nitrogen, 50 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potassium per hectare as furrow application. Gap fill at 7-10 days.
government_recommendation: Sow hybrid cotton at onset of southwest monsoon (June-July) or northeast monsoon (October-November) as per Tamil Nadu cotton zone recommendation.

guidance: At 15-20 days, thin to one plant per hill. Gap fill missing hills with raised nursery seedlings. Apply second nitrogen dose at 25 kg urea per hectare at 30 days. Use of plant growth regulator Mepiquat chloride at 2 ml per litre at 45 days controls excess vegetative growth.
government_recommendation: Apply plant growth regulator during squaring stage to prevent excessive vegetative growth and redirect energy toward boll formation.

guidance: Install pheromone traps for American bollworm at 5 traps per acre from 40 days. For sucking pests (aphids, jassids, thrips, whitefly), set up 5 yellow sticky traps per acre. If ETL (Economic Threshold Level) is reached: 8-10 moths per trap per week, spray Spinosad 45 SC at 0.3 ml per litre.
government_recommendation: Follow Cotton Scouting Program of TNAU: inspect 20 plants per acre twice weekly and record pest incidence to take timely spray decisions.

activity: Bacterial Blight and Alternaria Leaf Spot Monitoring
guidance: Scout for bacterial blight: angular water-soaked spots on leaves turning brown. Apply Copper Oxychloride 50 WP at 3 g per litre. For Alternaria leaf spot: circular brown spots with concentric rings. Spray Mancozeb 75 WP at 2 g per litre if incidence is above 10%.
government_recommendation: Grow disease-tolerant hybrid varieties and avoid overhead irrigation to reduce incidence of leaf diseases in cotton.

guidance: Monitor squaring and flowering from 45 days onwards. Apply potassium nitrate at 2% spray during flowering to improve boll set. Ensure adequate moisture during boll development. Remove young bolls affected by bollworm manually to prevent pest spread.
government_recommendation: Spray potassium nitrate 2% at squaring and boll development stages to improve boll retention and fibre quality as per TNAU advisory.

guidance: Stop irrigation 3 weeks before harvest. Apply Ethephon 500 ppm as defoliant to promote uniform boll opening if growing for mechanized picking. Monitor open boll percentage. Harvest when 60% bolls are open in the first picking.
government_recommendation: Avoid defoliant application unless mechanized harvesting is planned. Selective hand picking at 5-7 pickings maintains fibre quality.

guidance: Harvest cotton bolls in the morning when dew has dried. Use clean cotton bags to avoid contamination. Grade cotton as Fully Opened, Half Opened, and Stained. Do not mix different grades. Avoid polythene bags as they trap moisture and deteriorate fibre.
government_recommendation: Sell cotton at regulated cotton market yards (APMC) or through Tamil Nadu Government's cotton procurement centres to get MSP (Minimum Support Price).

guidance: Plough to 20-25 cm depth. Level field and form ridges at 60 cm spacing. Apply FYM at 12.5 tonnes per hectare. In Dharmapuri red loamy soils, apply lime at 500 kg per hectare to correct soil acidity if pH is below 6.0. Ensure good drainage.
government_recommendation: Conduct soil pH test before maize cultivation. Apply agricultural lime if pH is below 6.0 as maize grows best at pH 6.5-7.5.

guidance: Select high-yielding hybrids recommended for Tamil Nadu: COHM 5, COHM 6, NK 6240, or Pioneer 30V92. Treat seeds with Thiram at 3 g per kg seed and Azospirillum at 25 g per kg seed. Seed rate: 20 kg per hectare for hybrids, 25 kg for composite varieties.
government_recommendation: Use certified hybrid maize seeds from government-approved sources. Avoid farm-saved seeds of hybrids as they show reduced yield in second generation.

guidance: Sow seeds at 3-4 cm depth in ridges or flat beds. Maintain spacing of 60 cm between rows and 25 cm between plants. Apply basal fertilizer: 75 kg nitrogen, 75 kg phosphorus, and 75 kg potassium per hectare in furrows. Close furrows after fertilizer application before sowing.
government_recommendation: Apply Chlorpyrifos 1.5% dust at 25 kg per hectare in soil before sowing to prevent cutworm damage in Dharmapuri and Salem districts.

guidance: Thin plants to maintain 25 cm spacing at 15 days. Apply first nitrogen top dress at 75 kg urea per hectare at 25 days. Earth up rows at 30 days to provide support. Remove volunteer plants and rogues at 35 days. Ensure weed-free conditions till 40 days.
government_recommendation: Apply herbicide Atrazine 50 WP at 2 kg per hectare as pre-emergence spray within 3 days of sowing to control weeds effectively.

guidance: Critical stages for irrigation: germination, knee-high stage (25-30 days), tasselling (55-60 days), and grain filling (65-75 days). Total water requirement: 400-500 mm. Irrigate at 6-7 day intervals in summer. Avoid waterlogging as maize is sensitive to excess water.
government_recommendation: Never allow maize to experience water stress during tasselling and silk emergence stage as it directly reduces kernel set and grain yield.

guidance: Scout for Fall Armyworm (FAW) from 15 days: check whorl leaves for ragged holes with wet frass inside. Pull open whorl and check for worms. ETL: one egg mass or 5% plant damage per 20 plants. Apply Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG at 0.4 g per litre into whorl.
government_recommendation: Report Fall Armyworm outbreak to nearest Agricultural Extension Officer immediately. Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department has emergency spray schedule for FAW management.

guidance: Monitor tasselling (55-60 days) and silk emergence (60-65 days). Ensure no water stress during pollination. Dust maize tassels gently to assist pollination in closed areas. Spray 2% potassium nitrate at silking stage to improve kernel set. Remove barren plants.
government_recommendation: Avoid any pesticide spray during tasselling and silking to prevent disruption of pollination process.

guidance: Check black layer formation at base of kernel. Milk line should have moved to base of kernel. Husk colour turns from green to brown/pale. Moisture content at physiological maturity is 30-35%. Field dry to 20-22% moisture before mechanical harvesting.
government_recommendation: Harvest maize at correct moisture to prevent aflatoxin contamination especially in Dharmapuri and Salem districts where humid post-harvest conditions prevail.

guidance: Harvest when grain moisture is 20-22%. Use manual or mechanical combine harvester. Shell cobs immediately after harvest. Dry shelled grain to 12-13% moisture for safe storage. Clean and grade grain before storage. Remove cobs with mold or insect damage.
government_recommendation: Avail custom hiring of maize sheller from agricultural cooperative societies. Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department provides sheller subsidy under farm mechanization scheme.

guidance: Plough to 20-25 cm depth. Form raised beds of 120 cm width with 45 cm channel. In Krishnagiri red soil, apply lime at 2 tonnes per hectare to correct pH. Apply FYM at 25 tonnes per hectare and Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg per hectare. Ensure good drainage.
government_recommendation: Apply Trichoderma viride enriched compost as biological soil treatment to suppress soil-borne pathogens especially damping off and wilt diseases.

guidance: Prepare raised nursery beds. Sow seeds at 5 g per cent metre. Cover with fine sand and mulch with paddy straw. Irrigate with watering can twice daily. Apply Carbendazim 0.1% at 10 days to prevent damping off. Seedlings ready for transplanting at 25-30 days.
risk_factor: Damping Off; Leaf Miner in Nursery
government_recommendation: Use protrays with coco peat medium for nursery to produce healthier transplants. TNAU recommends pro-tray nursery for tomato to avoid transplanting shock.

guidance: Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings with ball of earth. Maintain spacing of 75 cm x 60 cm for indeterminate and 60 cm x 45 cm for determinate types. Irrigate immediately. Apply Carbofuran granules at 1 g per plant hole to protect against soil insects. Avoid transplanting during afternoon.
government_recommendation: Transplant tomato seedlings in the evening to reduce transplanting shock. Water every day for the first week after transplanting.

guidance: Stake indeterminate tomato plants with bamboo poles (1.5 m height) at 30-35 days after transplanting. Train plants to single or double stem. Apply first nitrogen dose at 30 kg urea per hectare at 20 days after transplanting. Remove suckers up to first fruiting branch.
expected_outcome: Healthy Vertical Growth; Better Air Circulation
government_recommendation: Staking is mandatory for indeterminate tomato varieties. Use jute twine for tying to avoid girdling and stem damage.

activity: Whitefly and Tomato Leaf Curl Virus Monitoring
guidance: Install yellow sticky traps at 5 per acre to monitor whitefly population. Inspect 20 plants per acre twice weekly for leaf curl symptoms (upward curling and yellowing of leaves). If more than 2 plants per 20 show virus symptoms, immediately rogue out and spray Imidacloprid 17.8 SL at 0.5 ml per litre.
government_recommendation: Grow TYLCV-tolerant varieties like PKM-1 and CO-3 in areas with high whitefly pressure in Krishnagiri and Vellore districts.

activity: Early Blight and Late Blight Monitoring
guidance: Scout for early blight: target-like concentric ring spots on older leaves. For late blight: dark water-soaked irregular spots on leaves with white fungal growth on underside. Apply Mancozeb 75 WP at 2 g per litre for early blight. Apply Metalaxyl-M 8 WP for late blight at 2.5 g per litre.
government_recommendation: Apply protective fungicide spray from 30 days after transplanting on weekly basis in Krishnagiri district where late blight is endemic due to cool night temperatures.

guidance: Apply boron at 0.2% foliar spray at flower initiation to prevent blossom drop. Spray Planofix (NAA) at 10 ppm during flowering to improve fruit set. Ensure soil moisture adequacy as water stress causes blossom end rot. Remove malformed flowers.
government_recommendation: Apply Calcium Nitrate at 1% foliar spray at fortnightly intervals to prevent blossom end rot especially in sandy soils of Salem district.

guidance: Harvest tomatoes at breaker stage (first colour break from green to pink/red) for distant markets. For local markets, harvest at red ripe stage. Withhold irrigation 3-4 days before harvest. Grade fruits as Grade I (above 65 g), Grade II (40-65 g), Grade III (below 40 g).
government_recommendation: Harvest at breaker stage for transportation to Chennai or distant markets. Tamil Nadu government provides cold storage subsidy for vegetable preservation.

guidance: Harvest tomatoes in the morning. Handle carefully to avoid bruising. Use clean plastic crates. Grade and pack in ventilated wooden boxes. Apply Thiabendazole post-harvest wash to extend shelf life. Do not expose harvested fruits to direct sunlight.
government_recommendation: Contact HOPCOMS (Horticultural Producers' Cooperative Marketing and Processing Society) for better marketing of tomatoes and access to government price stabilisation support.

guidance: Plough to 25-30 cm depth in hilly terrain of Nilgiris. Form ridges at 60 cm spacing. Apply FYM at 25 tonnes per hectare incorporated into ridges. Apply lime at 2 tonnes per hectare if pH is below 5.5. In Ooty areas, prepare terraced fields to prevent soil erosion.
government_recommendation: Follow contour farming practice in Nilgiris hills as recommended by Tamil Nadu Soil Conservation Department to prevent erosion and maintain soil fertility.

guidance: Use certified seed tubers from hills. Preferred varieties for Nilgiris: Kufri Jyoti, Kufri Muthu, Kufri Ooty-1. Select medium-sized tubers (40-60 g) with 2-3 eyes. Cut large tubers into pieces with one eye each. Treat cut pieces with Bordeaux paste to prevent rotting.
government_recommendation: Use certified seed potatoes from Tamil Nadu Seed Development Authority to ensure freedom from late blight

guidance: Plant sprouted seed tubers at 8-10 cm depth in ridges. Maintain spacing of 60 cm x 25 cm. Apply basal fertilizer: 100 kg nitrogen, 80 kg phosphorus, and 100 kg potassium per hectare. In Nilgiris cool climate, plant from August-October for best results.
government_recommendation: Plant potato in cool season (August-October) in Nilgiris and (November-January) in mid-elevation areas of Kodaikanal for maximum yield.

guidance: Carry out first earthing up at 20-25 days to cover developing tubers. Apply second nitrogen dose at 50 kg urea per hectare at 30 days. Irrigate at 7-10 day intervals. Maintain weed-free condition. Apply Mancozeb 75 WP preventively from 20th day for late blight protection.
government_recommendation: Apply second earthing up at 45 days to prevent greening of tubers which develops solanine toxin and reduces market quality.

guidance: Late blight is the most critical disease in Nilgiris. Scout twice weekly for water-soaked irregular lesions on leaves. Under cool humid conditions (below 18°C, RH above 85%), spray Cymoxanil + Mancozeb at 3 g per litre preventively every 7 days. Remove and destroy affected plants.
government_recommendation: Follow TNAU late blight forecasting system for Nilgiris district. Early warning alerts are issued by Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department for timely spray decisions.

guidance: At 80-85 days, check tuber maturity by rubbing skin with thumb. Mature tubers have set skin that does not peel off easily. Remove foliage by mechanical vine killing or Diquat spray at 3 ml per litre to hasten skin set. Wait 10-14 days before harvesting.
government_recommendation: Allow 10-14 days after vine death before harvesting to allow skin to set firmly which reduces storage losses and improves market quality.

guidance: Harvest with potato digger or fork. Avoid bruising and cutting. Sort out damaged, diseased, and greened tubers in the field. Grade by size: A grade (above 50 mm), B grade (35-50 mm), C grade (below 35 mm). Cure in shade for 5-7 days before storage or sale.
government_recommendation: Store potatoes in dark
column18: well-ventilated rooms to prevent greening. Tamil Nadu Horticulture Department provides cold storage subsidy in Nilgiris district.

guidance: Plough to 20-25 cm depth. Apply FYM at 12.5 tonnes per hectare. Form ridges at 60 cm spacing. In Vellore red loamy soils, apply gypsum at 400 kg per hectare to improve calcium and sulphur levels. Ensure good drainage as sunflower is sensitive to waterlogging.
government_recommendation: Deep summer ploughing followed by 2-3 harrowings ensures good tilth and helps in weed control for sunflower cultivation.

guidance: Select high oil content hybrid varieties: KBSH 44, MSFH 17, or CO 4 for Tamil Nadu conditions. These give oil content of 40-45%. Treat seeds with Thiram 75 WS at 3 g per kg. Inoculate with Azospirillum at 25 g per kg and PSB at 25 g per kg.
government_recommendation: Use hybrid sunflower seeds with oil content above 40% for better market value. TNAU recommends KBSH 44 for Tamil Nadu conditions.

guidance: Sow one seed per hill at 3-4 cm depth. Maintain spacing of 60 cm x 30 cm. Apply basal fertilizer: 60 kg nitrogen, 60 kg phosphorus, and 60 kg potassium per hectare. Seed rate: 5 kg per hectare for hybrids. Avoid sowing in water-stagnated areas.
government_recommendation: Sow sunflower at the beginning of northeast monsoon (October-November) in Tamil Nadu for best yield and oil content.

guidance: Thin to one plant per hill at 15 days. Apply first top dress nitrogen at 30 kg urea per hectare at 30 days after sowing. Earth up at 30 days. Hand weeding at 20 and 40 days. Apply Boron 0.2% foliar spray at bud stage to improve head formation.
government_recommendation: Apply boron foliar spray mandatorily at bud formation stage as sunflower is highly sensitive to boron deficiency affecting head and kernel development.

guidance: Install bee hives at 4 per acre during flowering for cross-pollination improvement. Shake plants early morning to assist self-pollination. Monitor for head borer (Helicoverpa) larvae inside developing head. Spray Carbaryl 50 WP at 2 g per litre if head borer incidence is above 5%.
government_recommendation: Install honey bee hives near sunflower fields during flowering as cross-pollination by bees can increase seed yield by 30-40%.

guidance: Heads are mature when back of head turns yellow-brown. Shield heads with bags if needed to prevent bird damage. Stop irrigation 10 days before harvest. Monitor for Alternaria blight on heads. Apply Mancozeb spray if needed to protect grain quality.
government_recommendation: Cover sunflower heads with perforated white paper bags when 10% heads show bird damage to prevent significant yield loss.

guidance: Harvest when 90% of heads turn brown and backs are yellow. Cut heads with 10-15 cm of stalk. Thresh and shell seeds. Dry to 9% moisture. Grade seeds and check for oil content. Transport to nearest oil mill or government cooperative.
government_recommendation: Contact Tamil Nadu Oilseeds Growers' Cooperative for MSP procurement of sunflower seeds to ensure fair price.

guidance: Plough to 15-20 cm depth. One deep ploughing and 2-3 cross harrowings. Apply FYM at 10 tonnes per hectare before last harrowing. In Ramanathapuram sandy loam soils apply 500 kg gypsum per hectare. Form field furrows for moisture conservation under rainfed conditions.
government_recommendation: Follow dryland agriculture practices recommended by TNAU for Ramanathapuram district: tie ridges at 50 m intervals for rainwater conservation.

guidance: Select drought-tolerant hybrids: CO 9, COHH 1, or TNAU Hybrid 1 for dry zone areas. These hybrids can withstand hot dry conditions. Treat seeds with Thiram 75 WS at 3 g per kg and Azospirillum at 25 g per kg. Seed rate: 3-4 kg per hectare for hybrids.
government_recommendation: Select Pearl Millet hybrids with downy mildew resistance for cultivation in Ramanathapuram and Sivagangai districts where disease is prevalent.

guidance: Sow at onset of rainy spell. Sow 3-4 seeds per hill at 3-4 cm depth on top of ridges. Maintain spacing of 45 cm x 15 cm. Apply 20 kg nitrogen and 40 kg phosphorus per hectare as basal. Thin to 2 plants per hill at 10 days. Gap fill missing hills.
government_recommendation: Sow Pearl Millet immediately after receipt of 20-25 mm rainfall for best germination under rainfed conditions.

guidance: Apply first nitrogen top dress at 20 kg urea per hectare at 20 days after sowing when adequate soil moisture is present. Hand weed at 20 and 35 days. Scout for shoot fly and stem borer. Apply Monocrotophos 36 SL at 1.5 ml per litre if shoot fly dead hearts exceed 5%.
government_recommendation: Apply nitrogenous fertilizer only when adequate soil moisture is available to prevent fertilizer burn in dry conditions.

activity: Shoot Fly and Stem Borer Monitoring
guidance: Inspect plants daily in the first 20 days for shoot fly damage (dead heart with foul smell). Count dead hearts per 20 plants. Apply Fipronil 0.3% GR at 25 kg per hectare in soil at sowing time. For stem borer, use pheromone traps at 5 per acre.
expected_outcome: Early Pest Detection; Reduced Crop Losses
government_recommendation: Integrated pest management using seed treatment with Chlorpyrifos followed by soil application of Carbofuran reduces shoot fly and stem borer damage effectively.

guidance: Monitor ear head emergence at 50-55 days. Ensure soil moisture during heading and grain filling. Apply second nitrogen at 20 kg urea per hectare at 25 days if available. Scout for ergot (pink sticky substance on ear heads) and blast (orange powder on spikelets).
government_recommendation: Scout for downy mildew (green ear disease) at early stage and destroy affected plants immediately to prevent spread in Ramanathapuram district.

guidance: Harvest when ear heads turn brown and grains are hard. Cut ear heads and dry in sun for 3-5 days. Thresh by hand or using mechanical thresher. Dry grain to safe moisture of 12%. Winnow and clean grain. Store in gunny bags in dry ventilated stores.
government_recommendation: Erect bird scaring devices from ear head emergence to prevent sparrow and parrot damage which can cause 15-20% yield loss in Pearl Millet.

guidance: Plough to 15-20 cm depth. Apply FYM at 12.5 tonnes per hectare. Level field. Finger millet can be sown by transplanting or direct seeding. For transplanting, prepare nursery beds and main field simultaneously. In Dharmapuri red soil, apply lime at 500 kg per hectare if pH is below 6.0.
government_recommendation: Finger Millet is highly tolerant to drought and soil acidity but lime application improves availability of nutrients in acidic soils of Dharmapuri district.

guidance: Select high-yielding varieties: CO 15, GPU 67, or ML 365 for Tamil Nadu conditions. For nursery: sow at 5 g per square metre in well-prepared nursery beds. Treat seeds with Thiram 3 g per kg. Nursery ready in 25 days. Main field prepared simultaneously.
government_recommendation: Apply Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g per litre as protective spray in nursery from 15th day to prevent blast disease.

guidance: Transplant 25-day seedlings in puddled field or well-irrigated field. Maintain spacing of 22.5 cm x 10 cm. Apply basal fertilizer: 50 kg nitrogen, 50 kg phosphorus, and 50 kg potassium per hectare. Transplant 2-3 seedlings per hill. Irrigate immediately after transplanting.
government_recommendation: Apply pre-emergence herbicide Pendimethalin at 3.3 litre per hectare after transplanting to control weeds in finger millet field.

guidance: Apply second nitrogen top dress at 25 kg urea per hectare at 30 days. Hand weed at 30 and 45 days. Earth up rows at 30 days. Monitor for blast disease on leaves and neck. Spray Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g per litre if blast lesions are observed on leaves.
government_recommendation: Nitrogen split application at basal
column18: and 60 days gives better yield than single application in finger millet.

guidance: Blast is the most critical disease of finger millet. Scout weekly for spindle-shaped lesions with grey centre on leaves. During humid weather, spray Tricyclazole 75 WP at 0.6 g per litre. Protect neck and ear head from blast. Critical periods: tillering and heading.
government_recommendation: Grow blast-resistant varieties GPU 67 and ML 365 in blast-endemic areas of Dharmapuri and Salem districts.

guidance: Harvest when ear heads turn brown and grains are hard. Cut heads with sickle. Dry in sun for 3-5 days. Thresh by trampling or mechanical thresher. Finger millet grain is very small, use fine-mesh sieve for cleaning. Dry to 12% moisture for safe storage.
government_recommendation: Finger millet grain stores well for long periods. Tamil Nadu farmers traditionally store finger millet in earthen pots and granaries for 3-5 years without pest problems.

guidance: Plough to 20-25 cm depth. One deep ploughing and 2 cross harrowings. Apply FYM at 10 tonnes per hectare. In Madurai black cotton soil, ridge and furrow method prevents waterlogging. Apply gypsum at 500 kg per hectare in saline-prone areas of Sivagangai.
government_recommendation: Sorghum can be grown in deep black cotton soil of Madurai and Theni districts which retains moisture for long periods reducing irrigation requirement.

guidance: Select improved varieties: CO 30, SPV 1411, or hybrid TNAU Sorghum 1. Treat seeds with Thiram 3 g per kg and Atrazine 50 WP 5 g per kg to control witchweed (Striga). Inoculate with Azospirillum at 25 g per kg. Seed rate: 10 kg per hectare for varieties.
government_recommendation: Apply herbicide Atrazine as seed treatment to control Striga (witchweed) which is a major constraint in rainfed sorghum of Madurai and Theni districts.

guidance: Sow 2 seeds per hill at 3-4 cm depth. Maintain spacing of 45 cm x 15 cm. Apply basal: 50 kg nitrogen, 50 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potassium per hectare. Thin to one plant per hill at 12 days. Gap fill within 10 days. Sow at onset of monsoon.
government_recommendation: Sow sorghum at recommended spacing for maximum yield. Wider spacing of 60x20 cm is recommended for kharif season to prevent diseases during humid conditions.

guidance: Apply first nitrogen top dress at 25 kg urea per hectare at 20 days. Apply second top dress at 25 kg urea per hectare at 40 days. Hand weed at 20 and 40 days. Monitor for shoot fly dead heart in early stage. Apply Endosulfan 35 EC at 1.5 ml per litre if shoot fly exceeds ETL.
government_recommendation: Apply split doses of nitrogen fertilizer during vegetative stage only when soil moisture is available to prevent fertilizer wastage in rainfed conditions.

guidance: Monitor head emergence at 65-70 days. Ensure adequate moisture during grain filling. Scout for head bug (mirid bug) and sorghum midge during flowering. Apply Dimethoate 30 EC at 2 ml per litre if head bug incidence exceeds 5 bugs per head.
government_recommendation: Monitor grain mold on sorghum head after flowering and apply protective fungicide if mold symptoms appear during humid post-flowering period.

guidance: Harvest when grain is hard and cannot be crushed with thumbnail. Cut ear heads and dry in sun. Thresh by trampling, beating, or mechanical thresher. Dry grain to 12% moisture. Clean and store in gunny bags. Sorghum grain stores well for 2-3 years with proper storage.
government_recommendation: Install bird scaring devices especially in sorghum fields adjacent to forests in Theni and Dindigul districts to prevent bird damage.

guidance: Dig pits of 1 m x 1 m x 1 m at spacing of 7.5 m x 7.5 m for tall varieties or 6 m x 6 m for dwarf varieties. In delta districts apply FYM at 50 kg per pit mixed with topsoil. Apply Neem cake at 5 kg per pit. Apply BHC 10% dust to prevent white grub damage.
government_recommendation: Pit preparation must be done 3 months before planting to allow soil weathering. Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department recommends square system planting for coconut.

guidance: Select 9-12 month old seedlings from certified nurseries. Seedling selection criteria: minimum 6 green leaves, collar girth above 10 cm, stout and healthy appearance. Preferred varieties: East Coast Tall for Delta areas, Chowghat Orange Dwarf for home gardens, hybrid COD x EC for high yield.
government_recommendation: Purchase coconut seedlings from Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department approved nurseries or TNAU coconut research station at Aliyarnagar.

guidance: Plant seedlings at centre of pit. Mix topsoil with FYM and half fill the pit. Place seedling with ball of earth. Fill remaining pit with topsoil-FYM mixture. Apply Sevidol at 50 g per pit to prevent root grub. Irrigate immediately. Shade young seedlings for first 3 months.
government_recommendation: Provide shade to newly planted coconut seedlings using palm fronds or shade net for the first 3-6 months to reduce transplanting stress.

guidance: Apply first dose of fertilizer at 6 months: 500 g each of urea, superphosphate, and muriate of potash per palm. Apply green manure crops between rows. Irrigate at 5-7 day intervals. Remove weeds in basin 2 m radius. Apply FYM at 25 kg per palm annually.
government_recommendation: Apply recommended dose of fertilizers to coconut in June and December as split application. Avoid application during water-stressed periods.

guidance: Adult coconut requires 45-90 litre per palm per day depending on climate. Install drip irrigation with 1 emitter of 8 LPH per palm. Critical stages: nut development and before summer. Avoid water stress during nut filling as it causes nut drop and reduces copra content.
expected_outcome: Improved Nut Yield and Copra Content
government_recommendation: Drip irrigation increases coconut yield by 20-25% and copra content by 15%. Government of Tamil Nadu provides subsidy on drip installation for coconut.

activity: Rhinoceros Beetle and Red Palm Weevil Monitoring
guidance: Inspect crown of coconut palms for V-shaped cuts on fronds caused by Rhinoceros beetle. Set up pheromone traps (Ethyl 4-methyloctanoate) at 1 per 4 palms for Red Palm Weevil monitoring. If weevil is detected, inject Monocrotophos 10 ml in 10 ml water at crown collar region.
government_recommendation: Pheromone traps are available through Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department at subsidized rates. Early detection of Red Palm Weevil through pheromone traps saves palms from fatal damage.

guidance: Root Wilt is a phytoplasma disease serious in Thanjavur and Tiruvarur districts. Symptoms: flaccidity of leaves, yellowing of outer whorl, nut shedding, and gradual decline. No cure once infected. Remove and burn infected palms. Apply Tetracycline trunk injection 5 g in 200 ml water in early stages.
government_recommendation: Avoid growing coconut in root wilt-endemic areas without proper disease management. Tamil Nadu Agriculture Department provides compensation for root wilt-affected palms under crop insurance scheme.

guidance: Harvest coconuts at 11-12 month age for copra making and at 8-9 months for tender coconut. Harvest at 45-day intervals. Use trained climbers or bamboo pole with sickle. Count harvest: healthy adult palm gives 60-100 nuts per year. Grade into tender nut, copra nut, and dried nut categories.
government_recommendation: Register with Tamil Nadu Coconut Development Board to avail various subsidy schemes and market support for coconut growers.

guidance: Before planting coffee, establish shade trees like silver oak (Grevillea robusta) at 8 m x 8 m spacing. Shade trees should be planted 2-3 years before coffee. In Nilgiris, existing forest shade is utilized. Dig trenches for contour planting to prevent soil erosion on slopes.
government_recommendation: Maintain optimum shade of 40-50% for Arabica coffee and 30-40% for Robusta. Excessive shade increases disease but insufficient shade causes sunscorch.

guidance: Raise coffee seedlings in polybags. Select Arabica varieties S.795, CxR, or Cauvery for quality. For Robusta, select S.274 or Sln. 6. Prepare nursery beds in shade. Sow parchment coffee at 2 cm depth. Seedlings ready in 9-12 months for transplanting.
risk_factor: Root Rot in Nursery; Antestia Bug
government_recommendation: Procure coffee seedlings from Coconut Board or Coffee Board certified nurseries to ensure varietal purity and disease freedom.

guidance: Plant 12-18 month old hardened seedlings in monsoon. Dig pits of 45 cm x 45 cm x 45 cm. Fill with topsoil and compost. Plant spacing: Arabica 2.5 m x 2.5 m, Robusta 3 m x 2.75 m. Mulch around seedlings with coffee pulp or leaf litter to conserve moisture.
government_recommendation: Apply mulch around coffee plants to conserve soil moisture during dry spell and improve soil organic matter over time.

guidance: Apply fertilizers at 300 g urea, 250 g superphosphate, and 150 g potassium chloride per plant per year in 3 splits. Carry out formative pruning to establish single stem and desired framework. Remove suckers below first primary branch. Spray copper fungicide after pruning wounds.
government_recommendation: Formative pruning during first 2 years determines future yield potential of coffee plant. Consult local Coffee Board officer for correct pruning technique.

activity: Coffee Berry Borer and White Stem Borer Monitoring
guidance: Scout for Coffee Berry Borer (small black beetle boring into coffee berries) from July-October. Apply Beauveria bassiana spray at 5 g per litre at berry formation. For white stem borer, inspect stem collars for frass and bore holes monthly. Apply Chlorpyrifos paste on collar region.
risk_factor: Coffee Berry Borer; White Stem Borer
government_recommendation: Use pheromone traps for Coffee Berry Borer monitoring. Coffee Board provides technical guidance and subsidized pheromone traps through district offices.

guidance: Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix) causes orange powdery lesions on lower leaf surface. Scout monthly. Apply Copper Oxychloride 50 WP at 3 g per litre after monsoon onset. Repeat at 30-day intervals. For severe infection use Propiconazole 25 EC at 1 ml per litre.
government_recommendation: Rust-resistant varieties like CxR and Cauvery have been developed by CCRI (Central Coffee Research Institute) and are recommended for Tamil Nadu coffee growing areas.

guidance: Harvest ripe red berries only (selective picking). Avoid stripping method as it reduces quality. Harvest during October-February in Tamil Nadu. Process by wet method (washed) for Arabica and dry method for Robusta. Primary processing within 24 hours of harvest.
government_recommendation: Practice selective red berry picking to maximize premium quality coffee output. Register with Coffee Board to avail minimum support price and market linkage.

guidance: Select well-drained hill slopes with good air drainage. Clear existing vegetation. Lay out contour trenches to prevent soil erosion. Prepare planting holes of 45 cm x 45 cm x 45 cm at spacing of 1.5 m x 1.5 m (square) or 1.2 m x 0.75 m (triangular) for high density planting.
government_recommendation: Plant tea on contour lines following Tamil Nadu Soil Conservation Department guidelines to prevent erosion in Nilgiris hill slopes.

guidance: Select clonal tea plants from authenticated nurseries. Best Nilgiris clones: UPASI 9, UPASI 17, UPASI 26 for high yield; BSS 1 and ATF series for quality. Use 18-month old hardened plants for transplanting. Clonal tea gives 30-40% higher yield than seedling tea.
government_recommendation: Source clonal planting material only from UPASI (United Planters' Association of South India) certified nurseries to ensure authenticity and disease-free status.

guidance: Plant clones in prepared holes during monsoon. Apply FYM at 2 kg per hole. Plant at correct depth (collar should be at ground level). Mulch around plants with paddy straw or weed biomass. Provide windbreak shading for 3-6 months after planting.
risk_factor: Transplanting Shock; Drought in Young Plants
government_recommendation: Provide temporary shade of 50% for newly transplanted tea clones using shade nets for the first 6 months to reduce moisture stress.

guidance: Apply formative pruning at 6 months to develop bushy growth. Journey pruning at 18 months to establish plucking table at 30-35 cm height. Apply fertilizers: 300 kg nitrogen, 75 kg phosphorus, and 75 kg potassium per hectare per year in 4 splits. Apply in March, June, September.
government_recommendation: Adopt recommended pruning cycle of 3-4 years (tipping to skiffing to pruning) to maintain productive plucking surface in Nilgiris tea estates.

guidance: Inspect tea shoots for Mosquito Bug damage (brown corky lesions on shoots). Install blue sticky traps at 10 per acre. If above ETL (5 bugs per shoot), apply Endosulfan 35 EC at 2 ml per litre. For red spider mite, apply Dicofol 18.5 EC at 2.5 ml per litre.
government_recommendation: Follow UPASI Nilgiris recommended IPM schedule for tea pest management. Avoid broad-spectrum pesticide application close to plucking to ensure tea safety standards.

guidance: Blister Blight is the most critical disease in Nilgiris tea. Scout weekly for pale yellow translucent spots turning to blisters on young shoots. Under humid conditions above 1000 m elevation, spray Copper Oxychloride 50 WP at 3 g per litre at 10-day intervals during monsoon.
government_recommendation: Preventive copper spray programme starting with onset of northeast monsoon is mandatory for Nilgiris tea to prevent blister blight epidemic.

guidance: Pluck young tea shoots at 7-10 day intervals during flush periods. Standard plucking: 2 leaves and a bud. Quality: coarse plucking (3 leaves and bud) for lower grade. Transport fresh leaves to factory within 4-6 hours of plucking in ventilated baskets. Do not compress leaves.
government_recommendation: Maintain plucking standards as per UPASI guidelines. Quality of tea depends 60% on standard of plucking (2 leaves and a bud) and 40% on factory processing.

guidance: Plough to 20 cm depth. Apply FYM at 25 tonnes per hectare and well-decomposed poultry manure at 5 tonnes per hectare. Form raised beds of 1.5 m width for transplanting or flat beds for sets planting. Apply Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg per hectare mixed with FYM.
government_recommendation: Deep ploughing in summer followed by solarisation using polythene mulch for 4 weeks reduces soil-borne diseases including white rot and basal rot significantly.

guidance: Prepare nursery beds of 1 m width. Sow seeds at 4 g per square metre. Cover with fine soil and mulch. Irrigate with watering can. Seedlings ready for transplanting at 40-45 days. Apply Carbendazim 0.1% at 15 days to prevent damping off. Thin overcrowded seedlings.
risk_factor: Damping Off; Purple Blotch in Nursery
government_recommendation: Ensure proper spacing in nursery beds to produce stout seedlings with pencil-thick stems that establish well after transplanting.

guidance: Transplant 40-45 day old seedlings at 15 cm x 10 cm spacing. Apply basal fertilizer: 50 kg nitrogen, 50 kg phosphorus, and 50 kg potassium per hectare. Irrigate immediately after transplanting. Remove damaged leaves before transplanting. Maintain rows to assist earthing up.
government_recommendation: Transplant onion seedlings in evening to reduce wilting stress. Apply root dip treatment with Carbendazim 0.1% solution before transplanting.

guidance: Apply second nitrogen dose at 25 kg urea per hectare at 30 days after transplanting. Earth up rows at 30-35 days to promote bulb development. Apply potassium chloride at 30 kg per hectare at 45 days. Maintain weed-free condition till 60 days for maximum bulb development.
government_recommendation: Avoid excess nitrogen after 45 days of transplanting as it delays bulb maturity and reduces storability of onion bulbs.

guidance: Thrips are major pest of onion. Check leaf damage (silver streaks on inner leaf surface) and count thrips per leaf. Yellow sticky traps at 5 per acre for monitoring. If above ETL (5 thrips per leaf), spray Spinosad 45 SC at 0.3 ml per litre with sticker agent.
government_recommendation: Add sticker (Teepol or soap solution at 1 ml per litre) to all pesticide sprays on onion to improve coverage on smooth waxy leaves.

activity: Purple Blotch and Stemphylium Blight Monitoring
guidance: Scout for purple blotch: white spots with purple centre on leaves. For Stemphylium blight: water-soaked spots turning brown. Apply Mancozeb 75 WP at 2 g per litre at 15-day intervals from 30 days after transplanting. Alternate with Iprodione 50 WP at 2 g per litre.
government_recommendation: Purple blotch is the most common foliar disease of onion in Tamil Nadu. Preventive fungicide spray schedule starting at 30 days after transplanting gives effective control.

guidance: Harvest when 50-75% of tops fall over naturally. Avoid harvesting very early as it reduces yield and quality. Withhold irrigation 10 days before harvest. Test maturity: outer scales should be dry and papery. Bulb neck should be soft and closed for good storability.
government_recommendation: Withhold irrigation 10 days before harvest to improve bulb curing and reduce neck rot during storage. Avoid harvesting immature bulbs.

guidance: Harvest bulbs using hand fork or tractor-mounted digger. Dry in windrows for 3-5 days with tops covering bulbs. After field curing, clip tops 2 cm above neck. Grade by size: Super (above 60 mm), Large (45-60 mm), Medium (25-45 mm). Pack in jute bags.
government_recommendation: Dry onion bulbs in shade after harvest for uniform curing to improve shelf life and storage quality. Contact NAFED for MSP procurement of onion during market glut.

guidance: Plough to 25 cm depth. Apply FYM at 25 tonnes per hectare. Form raised beds of 1.2 m width with furrows. Apply Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg per hectare as biocontrol agent. In Erode red soils, apply lime if pH is below 6.0. Ensure good drainage.
government_recommendation: Sandy loam to clay loam soils with good drainage are ideal for chilli cultivation. Avoid heavy clay soils as they cause waterlogging and Phytophthora root rot.

guidance: Prepare raised nursery beds. Treat soil with Formaldehyde 40% diluted 1:49 and cover with polythene for 2 days for soil sterilization. Sow seeds at 1 g per metre row. Apply Carbendazim 0.1% to prevent damping off. Seedlings ready at 35-40 days.
government_recommendation: Install 50 mesh nylon net insect screen around nursery to protect seedlings from thrips and whitefly that transmit Chilli Leaf Curl Virus.

guidance: Transplant 35-40 day old seedlings at 75 cm x 60 cm spacing. Apply Imidacloprid 17.8 SL at 0.5 ml per litre as root dip for 30 minutes before transplanting to protect against thrips and whitefly. Irrigate immediately. Shade for 3 days after transplanting.
government_recommendation: Treat chilli seedling roots with Imidacloprid before transplanting as a systemic protection against thrips and whitefly that transmit leaf curl virus.

guidance: Stake tall chilli varieties at 60 days. Apply split dose nitrogen: 25 kg urea at 30 days and 25 kg at 60 days after transplanting. Apply potassium at 30 kg MOP per hectare at 45 days. Remove early flower buds for first 25 days to build vegetative frame.
government_recommendation: Apply micronutrient mixture foliar spray (zinc
column18: molybdenum) at 30 days after transplanting to prevent micronutrient deficiency symptoms common in Erode soils.

guidance: Set yellow sticky traps at 5 per acre for whitefly monitoring and blue traps for thrips. Inspect 20 plants per acre twice weekly. For broad mite (leaf distortion on shoots), apply Dicofol 18.5 EC at 2.5 ml per litre. For thrips spray Spinosad 45 SC at 0.3 ml per litre.
government_recommendation: Broad mite (Polyphagotarsonemus latus) causes severe distortion of chilli leaves and is often confused with virus symptoms. Use hand lens for identification before spraying.

guidance: Scout for anthracnose: sunken water-soaked spots on fruits with orange spore mass. Apply Carbendazim 0.1% spray at 14-day intervals. For powdery mildew: white powdery coating on leaves. Spray wettable sulphur 80 WP at 3 g per litre. Scout weekly.
government_recommendation: Anthracnose fruit rot is the most critical disease of chilli in Tamil Nadu causing 30-40% yield loss. Preventive spray programme during fruiting stage is essential.

guidance: Harvest chillies at green stage for fresh market (65-70 days after transplanting) or at red ripe stage for dry chilli market (90-120 days). Harvest every 10-15 days. Handle with gloves to prevent skin irritation. Grade by size and colour. Dry red chillies in sun on clean surfaces.
government_recommendation: Dry chillies to safe moisture of 10% to prevent mold growth and aflatoxin contamination. Store in moisture-proof bags or gunny bags with silica gel.

guidance: Plough to 20-25 cm depth. Apply FYM at 25 tonnes per hectare. Form raised beds of 1.2 m width. Apply Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg per hectare. Add neem cake at 200 kg per hectare for nematode and soil pest control. Ensure good drainage.
government_recommendation: Apply neem cake as soil treatment to manage root-knot nematode which is a serious constraint in brinjal cultivation in light sandy soils of Vellore district.

guidance: Sow brinjal seeds at 1 g per metre row in sterilized nursery beds. Apply Carbendazim 0.1% at 10 days to prevent damping off. Seedlings ready at 25-30 days. Water twice daily. Apply Azospirillum and PSB as nursery bed treatment for biofertilizer benefits.
government_recommendation: Use raised nursery beds in brinjal to prevent damping off which is common during wet season in Tamil Nadu. Sterilize nursery soil before sowing.

guidance: Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings at 75 cm x 60 cm spacing. Apply Carbofuran at 25 g per hill at planting hole for nematode and stem borer control. Irrigate immediately. Stake tall varieties. Apply Carbendazim 0.1% root dip before transplanting.
government_recommendation: Use nematode-resistant rootstock grafting technique for brinjal in nematode-endemic areas as recommended by TNAU for Vellore district.

guidance: Shoot and Fruit Borer (Leucinodes orbonalis) is the most critical pest of brinjal. Install pheromone traps at 5 per acre from 20 days. Cut and destroy dead shoots daily. Apply Emamectin Benzoate 5 SG at 0.4 g per litre at 10-day intervals during fruiting stage.
government_recommendation: Release Trichogramma chilonis egg cards at 5 cards per hectare per week during peak flowering stage for biological control of brinjal shoot and fruit borer.

guidance: Harvest brinjal fruits at tender stage (before seeds harden) every 5-7 days. Fruits should be shiny and firm. Use sharp knife or pruning shear. Grade: Super grade (uniform size, no damage), Regular grade (minor blemishes). Market in ventilated bamboo baskets to prevent bruising.
government_recommendation: Regular harvesting every 5-7 days improves total yield by maintaining plant vigour. Avoid delayed harvest as it reduces fruit quality and plant productivity.

guidance: Plough to 20-25 cm depth. Apply FYM at 20 tonnes per hectare. Level and form ridges at 45 cm spacing. Apply Trichoderma viride at 2.5 kg per hectare mixed with FYM for soil-borne disease management. In sandy soils of Vellore district, apply neem cake at 250 kg per hectare.
government_recommendation: Okra can be grown year-round in Tamil Nadu. Kharif (June-July) and summer (January-February) crops are most common in Vellore and Salem districts.

guidance: Select hybrids: Arka Anamika, CO 1, Varsha Uphar, or Kashi Vibhuti for Tamil Nadu. Treat seeds with Thiram 3 g per kg. Soak seeds in water for 12 hours before sowing to improve germination rate. Inoculate with Azospirillum and PSB at 25 g each per kg seed.
government_recommendation: Choose YVMV (Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus) resistant okra varieties for areas with high whitefly pressure to prevent crop failure from virus disease.

guidance: Sow 2 seeds per hill at 2-3 cm depth. Maintain spacing of 45 cm x 30 cm. Apply basal fertilizer: 25 kg nitrogen, 25 kg phosphorus, and 25 kg potassium per hectare. Thin to one plant per hill at 10-12 days. Gap fill missing hills within 10 days.
government_recommendation: Do not sow okra seeds deeper than 3 cm as it reduces germination. Shallow sowing ensures faster emergence especially in heavy soils.

guidance: Apply first nitrogen top dress at 15 kg urea per hectare at 20 days after sowing. Hand weed at 20 and 35 days. Monitor for whitefly and yellow vein mosaic virus. Remove and destroy virus-infected plants immediately. Apply Imidacloprid 17.8 SL at 0.5 ml per litre to control whitefly.
government_recommendation: Rogue out YVMV (Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus) infected plants as soon as symptoms appear to prevent spread through whitefly vectors.

guidance: Install yellow sticky traps at 5 per acre for whitefly monitoring. Inspect plants daily for shoot borer damage. If shoot borer incidence above 5%, apply Quinalphos 25 EC at 2 ml per litre. Alternately apply Neem Oil 2% spray for organic management.
government_recommendation: Maintain field sanitation by removing alternate weed hosts of whitefly around okra fields to reduce virus disease pressure.

guidance: Harvest okra pods at tender stage: 5-7 days after flower opening, when 8-10 cm long. Harvesting every 2-3 days maintains tenderness. Use gloves to avoid skin irritation from trichomes. Grade: A grade (8-10 cm, light green, tender), B grade (10-12 cm). Pack in cool ventilated boxes.
government_recommendation: Okra turns fibrous within 2-3 days of optimum harvest stage. Harvest regularly every 2 days to maintain tender quality and ensure continuous yield.

activity: Pit or Bed Preparation for Turmeric
guidance: Plough to 25-30 cm depth. Apply FYM at 25 tonnes per hectare and neem cake at 2 tonnes per hectare. Form raised beds of 1 m width and 20 cm height or flat beds for irrigated conditions. In Erode red loamy soils, add gypsum at 400 kg per hectare for sulphur requirement.
government_recommendation: Erode district is the major turmeric producing area in Tamil Nadu. Deep bed preparation with neem cake incorporation reduces rhizome rot and nematode problems significantly.

guidance: Select healthy mother rhizomes of 50-70 g weight with 2-3 buds from disease-free crop. Preferred varieties: Erode Local, BSR 1, CO 1, Sugandham. Treat rhizomes with Mancozeb 0.3% for 30 minutes and dry in shade before planting. Apply Trichoderma viride 10 g per kg as bio-treatment.
government_recommendation: Use rhizomes from BSR 1 and CO 1 varieties that give high curcumin content (4-5%) preferred by spice processing industry in Erode district.

guidance: Plant rhizomes at 5-7 cm depth in furrows or pits. Maintain spacing of 30 cm x 20 cm. Apply basal fertilizer: 60 kg nitrogen, 60 kg phosphorus, and 120 kg potassium per hectare. Cover with soil and mulch with paddy straw or sugarcane trash at 10 tonnes per hectare.
government_recommendation: Mulching with paddy straw or sugarcane trash after planting conserves soil moisture
column18: and maintains soil temperature for better rhizome sprouting.

guidance: Apply second nitrogen dose at 30 kg urea per hectare at 60 days. Third dose at 30 kg urea per hectare at 120 days. Earth up rows at 40-45 days to encourage new rhizome development. Irrigate at 7-10 day intervals. Remove weeds regularly. Replenish mulch as it decomposes.
government_recommendation: Apply potassium in 3 split doses: at planting
column18: and at 90 days to ensure continuous potassium availability for rhizome filling.

activity: Rhizome Rot and Leaf Blotch Monitoring
guidance: Scout for rhizome rot: yellowing and wilting of leaves with brown discolouration of stem at soil level. Remove and destroy affected plants. Drench soil around affected areas with Copper Oxychloride 0.3% solution. For leaf blotch: oval brown spots on leaves, spray Mancozeb 0.2%.
government_recommendation: Avoid waterlogging in turmeric field as it is the primary cause of rhizome rot. Ensure proper drainage especially during monsoon season.

guidance: Harvest turmeric when leaves turn yellow and stems begin to dry. This occurs at 8-9 months after planting. Stop irrigation 2 weeks before harvest. Conduct test harvest of 5 clumps to check rhizome development. Curcumin content is maximum at this stage.
expected_outcome: Maximum Curcumin Content; Good Rhizome Yield
government_recommendation: Harvest turmeric at correct maturity (8-9 months) to get maximum curcumin content which determines market price in Erode spice market.

guidance: Harvest by digging clumps with spade or fork. Separate mother rhizomes (seed purpose) from fingers (commercial purpose). Boil fingers in water for 45-60 minutes until soft froth appears. Dry on clean floor for 10-15 days until moisture reduces to 10-12%. Polish in drum polisher or manually.
expected_outcome: High Quality Dry Turmeric for Market
government_recommendation: Cure turmeric by boiling within 2-3 days of harvest. Delayed boiling reduces curcumin content and market quality. Erode turmeric market sets quality standards for national and export markets.
